story.hook: My building app said someone was calling the elevator to my floor every night while I was still at work.
story.like_cta: LIKE IF THAT WOULD CREEP YOU OUT
story.premise: A woman keeps receiving elevator notifications saying her apartment floor was selected while she is away from home.
story.punchline: Someone wasn't visiting my apartment every night. My forgotten accessibility setting was taking phantom elevator rides.
story.script: The notification looked harmless: Elevator request completed, floor twelve. The problem was I was twenty minutes away from home. The next evening it happened again. Then again. Always between six and seven. My apartment door sensor showed nobody entering, but I started imagining someone wandering the hallway outside. I asked security whether they could check visitor records. No visitor had registered for me. They reviewed the elevator camera and saw delivery riders, residents, cleaners, nothing obviously connected to my unit. The building app said every request came through my resident profile, which made it even stranger. I changed my password. The notifications continued. Management disabled my mobile elevator access for a day. Another floor-twelve request appeared anyway. That finally proved it wasn't my phone. A technician checked the access-control system and found a second device linked to my profile: an accessibility call button in the lobby. Months earlier I'd injured my ankle and management temporarily paired that button with my floor so I could summon an elevator without reaching the touchscreen while using crutches. After I recovered, everyone forgot to remove the pairing. But why was it suddenly being pressed every evening? We watched the lobby camera again, this time looking at the button instead of the elevator. A grocery delivery worker rolled in with a large cart, pressed it, and waited. He did the same thing on three different nights. He wasn't trying to reach my floor. He had discovered that the accessibility button held the elevator doors open longer, which made loading his cart easier. Because the button was still paired with my old profile, the system also preselected floor twelve and sent me a notification. He usually canceled the floor once inside and went wherever the actual customer lived. Management unpaired my account and configured the button properly for general accessibility use. I felt slightly ridiculous for imagining a mystery visitor stalking my hallway. The delivery guy had never even been to my floor. Someone wasn't visiting my apartment every night. My forgotten accessibility setting was taking phantom elevator rides.
story.twist: Her profile is still linked to a temporary accessibility button near the lobby, and a delivery worker has been using that button because it holds the elevator doors longer for his cart.

youtube.description: Nightly elevator alerts make one resident think someone is visiting her floor until an old accessibility setting resurfaces. #WackyDramas #Shorts
youtube.title: My Elevator App Said Someone Kept Visiting My Floor
